faqs.q: How do I convert a PNG to SVG?

faqs.a: With 2 colors the tool thresholds the brightness: everything darker than your threshold becomes black vector shapes. It is ideal for logos, stamps, and line art.
The tracer quantizes the image into your chosen number of dominant colors, traces each color region separately, and stacks them as filled vector paths — a simplified, stylized version of the photo.

faqs.q: Will the SVG look exactly like my photo?

faqs.a: Yes. SVG is resolution-independent, so the traced file scales from favicon to billboard with zero quality loss.

image-to-svg-converter.formula:
case = TL + 2·TR + 4·BR + 8·BL   (marching-squares, 16 cases)
path = DouglasPeucker(polyline, ε)
output = Σ filled paths, one per color layer, fill-rule evenodd
howTo: Upload the raster image (PNG or JPG) you want to vectorize.
Choose 2 colors for a black silhouette trace, or 3–6 colors for a stylized color trace.
Set the trace detail (image is downsampled to this size) and the smoothing amount.
Watch the live vector preview update as you adjust the sliders.
Press Download SVG to save the file, or Copy SVG code to paste it elsewhere.
keyFacts: The image is downsampled to your detail setting (200–600 px) before tracing, which keeps tracing fast.
Marching squares scans every 2 × 2 pixel cell and draws contour segments for 16 possible cases.
Segments are joined into polygons, simplified with the Douglas-Peucker algorithm, and emitted as SVG paths.
With 2 colors, brightness below your threshold becomes the traced shape; with 3–6, the dominant colors are quantized and traced per layer.
Tiny specks below 4 px² are dropped automatically to keep the SVG clean.

image-to-svg-converter.workedExample:
A 400 × 300 px logo traced at detail 400 with 2 colors and threshold 128:
cells scanned = 400 × 300 = 120,000 (16 marching-squares cases each)
Every pixel darker than brightness 128 becomes part of the black mask; the mask boundary is converted to polygons, simplified, and written as SVG paths.
The result scales from a 16 px favicon to a poster with zero quality loss.
